title: Classes and Objects
description: Create your own kind of thing with a class, then make objects from it.

content.value: A class is a blueprint for making things. Think of a cookie cutter: you make the cutter once, then use it to stamp out many cookies that all share the same shape. In Python, the blueprint is a class, and each thing you make from it is an object.
You create a class with the `class` keyword. Inside, you can store data (called attributes) and define actions (called methods, which are just functions that belong to the class).
To make an object from a class, write the class name with parentheses and pass in the data. Each object is separate and keeps its own values.

dog1 = Dog("Buddy", "Golden Retriever")
dog2 = Dog("Max", "Pug")

print(dog1.name)  # Prints Buddy
dog2.bark()       # Prints Max says Woof!
Notice the word `self` in the methods. Python uses `self` to mean 'this particular object', so each dog can use its own name and breed.

practice.question: Using the Dog class below, make a Dog object named 'rover' with breed 'Labrador', then call rover.bark().

quiz.question: What is a class in Python?
quiz.explain: A class is a blueprint. From one blueprint you can make many objects, like one cookie cutter makes many cookies.

quiz.question: What do we call the actions defined inside a class?
quiz.explain: Actions inside a class are called methods. The data it stores (like a name or color) are called attributes.
